newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN GOVT REMOVES FOREIGN LIMITS ON OPTUS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN GOVT REMOVES FOREIGN LIMITS ON OPTUS.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday he was removing the foreign ownership restrictions on telecoms companies Optus Communications and Vodaphone Australia.
"The government considers that it is no longer necessary to constrain foreign involvement in Optus and Vodaphone," Costello said in a statement.

Foreign shareholdings in Optus were previously limited to 49 percent with British telecoms company Cable & Wireless Plc and United States-based BellSouth Corp both holding 24.5 percent of the company.

But in July, Cable & Wireless (C&W) bought out BellSouth's holding for about A$980 million and said it planned to further increase its stake to around 51.5 percent by exercising options at a price of A$565 million.
"In consequence of this change in policy, the government has now approved the foreign investment application from C&W to increase its investment in Optus," Costello said.

Costello said the level of foreign ownership of Optus and Vodafone would now be open, although applications from foreign companies to lift their holdings would be subject to Foreign Investment Review Board approval.
Under the previous rules, Vodafone Australia was required to achieve majority local ownership by July 1, 2003, but this was no longer necessary, a government spokesman said.
